headline: BLUE STAR FILES NI 43-101 AT ULU — 558KOZ M+I AT 7.87 G/T, NUNAVUT DIG GRANT ADDS AUMA DRILL FUNDING (TSXV:BAU)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Blue Star Gold Corp. (TSXV:BAU)
snippet: Blue Star Gold Corp. (TSXV:BAU) announced July 7, 2026 two catalysts simultaneously: the filing of the NI 43-101 technical report on its Ulu Gold Project in Nunavut — reporting measured and indicated resources of 558,000 oz at 7.87 g/t Au and inferred resources of 476,000 oz at 4.54 g/t Au — and the award of up to C$250,000 from Nunavut's Discovery, Invest and Grow (DIG) program to fund 2026 drilling at the adjacent Auma Project. The dual announcement marks a transition from resource delineation at Ulu to active exploration at a second project on the same landholding, with Nunavut DIG funding providing non-dilutive capital and the filed technical report establishing the formal resource base that institutional investors require before committing capital.

headline: FOMC MINUTES DROP WEDNESDAY — WARSH'S WITHHELD DOT PLOT EXPOSES 9-9 RATE SPLIT AS GOLD AWAITS SEPTEMBER VERDICT
snippet: GoldSilver.com's July 7, 2026 market preview frames Wednesday's release of the June 16-17 FOMC minutes as the next key catalyst for gold: the minutes will confirm whether Fed Chair Warsh's historically unprecedented decision to withhold his 2026 rate-path dot-plot projection — the first Fed chair to do so since the dot plot was introduced in 2012 — reflects a genuine 9-9 split on further hikes that markets have not fully priced. With CME FedWatch pegging September hike odds at 50-55% following the June NFP miss (57,000 jobs vs 113,000 consensus) and gold at $4,148, any signal from the minutes confirming a genuine hold consensus would compress real yields and catalyse the next leg of gold's recovery, while a hawkish reading of the vote split could pressure the metal below current support.

headline: SPANISH MOUNTAIN HITS 69M AT 0.74 G/T — WHEATON-BACKED CARIBOO FEASIBILITY ADDS 2 RIGS TO 60,000M CAMPAIGN (TSXV:SPA)
source_name: Business Wire / Spanish Mountain Gold Ltd. (TSXV:SPA)
snippet: Spanish Mountain Gold Ltd. (TSXV:SPA) reported July 6, 2026 new assay results from its feasibility study drill program at the Spanish Mountain Gold Project in British Columbia's Cariboo Gold Corridor — highlights include 69.20 metres at 0.74 g/t Au and 77.85 metres at 0.70 g/t Au as part of a 60,000-metre total campaign now 16,083 metres complete, with two additional rigs arriving the week of July 8 to accelerate data collection. The program is underpinned by Wheaton Precious Metals' $55 million advance for a 1.5% NSR royalty — a royalty-backed financing structure that signals institutional confidence in the project's economics ahead of a construction decision targeted for 2028, and one of the largest non-dilutive financing commitments to a British Columbia bulk-tonnage gold developer in the current cycle.

headline: XXIX CLEARS ONTARIO PERMIT FOR FIRST THIERRY DRILL IN 40 YEARS — 20,000M TARGETS K1 BULK COPPER-PGE SYSTEM (TSXV:XXIX)
source_name: Investing News Network / XXIX Metal Corp. (TSXV:XXIX)
snippet: XXIX Metal Corp. (TSXV:XXIX) received its exploration permit from the Province of Ontario on July 6, 2026 for the Thierry Copper Project near Pickle Lake, Ontario — authorizing the first large-scale drill program in over 40 years at what XXIX describes as Ontario's largest primary copper resource, a deposit with historical production of 5.8 million tonnes at 1.13% copper. The permit unlocks a two-phase 20,000-metre program targeting K1, now reinterpreted as a single near-surface disseminated bulk-tonnage copper-PGE system measuring approximately 1.4 km of strike by 250 m wide to 400 m depth and open at depth — XXIX enters drill season with over $19 million in cash and approximately $24 million in working capital following a $17.2 million financing, making this a fully funded program at a structurally significant deposit that went undrilled for a generation due to ownership fragmentation.

headline: ROSE WEST DRILL HALTED BY FOREST FIRE — CRITICAL ELEMENTS 11 HOLES IN WHEN SOPFEU PROXIMITY FORCES SUSPENSION (TSXV:CRE)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Critical Elements Lithium Corp. (TSXV:CRE)
snippet: Critical Elements Lithium Corp. (TSXV:CRE) reported July 6, 2026 that a proximal forest fire has temporarily suspended drilling at its 10,000-metre Phase 2 Summer 2026 program at the Rose West lithium discovery in Quebec, with SOPFEU (Quebec's wildfire agency) consultation prompting evacuation of crews after 11 holes totalling 2,073 metres were completed. Phase 1 Winter 2026 drilling had already expanded the mineralized footprint from 450m x 370m to 1,250m x 800m at 10-40m typical spodumene-bearing pegmatite thickness — the forest fire interruption is operationally temporary but illustrates the seasonal wildfire risk that affects all Boreal Quebec lithium programs in summer, a factor investors in Northern Quebec explorers must incorporate into timeline planning for the H2 2026 field season.

headline: KING COPPER DIA APPROVED: 36,010M COLQUEMAYO DRILL CLEARS PERU ENVIRONMENTAL HURDLE — FIRST HOLES IMMINENT (TSXV:KCP)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / King Copper Discovery Corp. (TSXV:KCP)
snippet: King Copper Discovery Corp. (TSXV:KCP) received Peruvian environmental impact approval — a Declaracion de Impacto Ambiental (DIA) — on July 6, 2026 for its Colquemayo Project in southern Peru, authorizing up to 36,010 metres of diamond drilling from 40 platforms across 59 holes and advancing the project to the resource estimation stage. The DIA is the primary environmental certification required for exploration-stage drilling in Peru, and its receipt clears the last regulatory milestone before drill mobilization — Colquemayo enters drill-ready status in one of South America's most prolific copper belts at a moment when global copper scarcity and US tariff-driven supply chain disruption are driving sustained investor attention to new primary copper discoveries outside China-controlled supply chains.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD ACQUIRES LOST LAKE IN GOLD ROCK CAMP — 123 CLAIMS CONSOLIDATE DISTRICT AROUND EXISTING HOLDINGS (TSXV:DRY)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Dryden Gold Corp. (TSXV:DRY)
snippet: Dryden Gold Corp. (TSXV:DRY) announced July 6, 2026 that it has entered into an option agreement to acquire 100% of 123 mineral claims comprising the Lost Lake Property from Orebot Inc. for C$100,000 cash and 125,000 common shares payable over two years, plus a 3% NSR (half buyable for $1 million), surrounding the company's existing Gold Rock Mining Camp claims in Northwestern Ontario. The Lost Lake claims target orogenic gold mineralization in brittle-ductile deformation zones of the Manitou-Dinorwic Deformation Zone — Dryden is backed by Centerra Gold and Alamos Gold as strategic investors, and continued district consolidation by a major-producer-backed junior at $4,100+ gold mirrors the acquisition patterns that historically precede formal joint ventures or takeout approaches.

headline: STATE STREET, GOLDMAN, UBS AND WGC AGREE: GOLD Q2 SELLOFF CHANGED THE PRICE, NOT THE THESIS
snippet: A July 7, 2026 GoldSilver.com analysis synthesises fresh institutional commentary from State Street, Goldman Sachs, the World Gold Council, UBS, and MKS PAMP following gold's Q2 2026 selloff — in which the metal fell from its January all-time high of $5,405 to a June 24 corrective low of $3,993, its worst quarter in 13 years — with all five institutions concluding the selloff reset the entry price rather than invalidating the multi-year bull thesis. The consistent message across five independent research teams — that central bank buying, structural portfolio allocation, and the real yield trajectory remain intact — establishes a broad institutional consensus that the Q2 correction was a cyclical pause within a secular bull market, a framing that has historically proven accurate when multiple major institutions simultaneously reaffirm a commodity direction after a sharp drawdown.

headline: TALAMORE LOCKS IN C$620M FOR COFFEE MINE, YUKON — C$100M EQUITY CLOSING JULY 21, EARLY WORKS UNDERWAY (TSXV:TALA)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Talamore Mining Corp. (TSXV:TALA)
snippet: Talamore Mining Corp. (TSXV:TALA) announced July 5, 2026 a construction financing package for its 100%-owned Coffee Gold Project in Yukon Territory — comprising a C$100 million equity offering (Stifel and BMO joint bookrunners, targeted close approximately July 21), a C$100 million debt facility, C$88 million in anticipated warrant exercises, and existing cash, with early works construction already underway and full construction launch targeted for H1 2027. Coffee is one of a small number of fully permitted Canadian gold development projects announcing formal construction financing in the current environment — the Stifel/BMO-led institutional equity tranche, simultaneous debt commitment, and warrant uptake together signal real institutional market appetite for pure-play Canadian Tier-1 jurisdiction gold construction stories at $4,100+ gold.

headline: JPMORGAN CUTS GOLD Q4 TO $4,500 — 25% REDUCTION CITES FED RISK, BUT CENTRAL BANK BUYING KEEPS BULL CASE INTACT
snippet: JPMorgan's commodities research desk cut its Q4 2026 gold price forecast by approximately 25% to $4,500 per ounce in early July 2026, abandoning an earlier $6,000 year-end target and citing the risk that stronger-than-expected US summer economic data could reignite Federal Reserve rate hike expectations — identifying $3,500-$3,600 as the potential downside scenario if September hike probability reaches certainty. The bank maintained its long-term bullish thesis underpinned by structural central bank demand and growing portfolio allocation trends, framing the forecast revision as a near-term risk adjustment rather than a thesis change — context that matters directly to junior mining investors modelling project economics, as many project NPV models benchmark gold across the $3,500-$4,500 range that JPMorgan now frames as the 2026 probability corridor.
